back: Costing work done to a customer's order, with a job cost sheet recording materials, labour, expenses and absorbed overhead.
Costing a quantity of identical units made together; cost per unit = batch cost ÷ units produced.
For a single standard product: total cost of the period ÷ units produced.
Cost × (1 + mark-up %). Mark-up is a percentage of cost.
Cost ÷ (1 - margin %). Margin is a percentage of the selling price.
A 25% mark-up equals a 20% margin; a 50% mark-up equals a 33.3% margin.
Direct materials, direct labour, direct expenses = prime cost; add absorbed production overhead = production cost; add other overheads = total cost.
Set-up cost is incurred once per batch, so a larger batch gives a lower set-up cost per unit.
Contract costing and process costing are not examined.
